blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: Not Always Equal
blocks.content: Equations (=) demand perfection: x MUST be exactly 5. But **Inequalities** are flexible. They say things like 'x must be MORE than 3' (x > 3) or 'x can be anything up to 10' (x <= 10). In real life, inequalities are everywhere: speed limits (v <= 60), minimum ages (age >= 18), and budget constraints (cost < 500).

blocks.title: 2. The Rules: The Four Symbols
blocks.content:
Master these four:

• **>** means 'greater than' (strict, not equal).
• **<** means 'less than' (strict, not equal).
• **>=** means 'greater than or equal to'.
• **<=** means 'less than or equal to'.

The critical rule: if you MULTIPLY or DIVIDE both sides by a NEGATIVE number, you must FLIP the inequality sign! (e.g., > becomes <).

blocks.title: 3. Step-by-Step: Solving Inequalities
blocks.content:
Solve inequalities exactly like equations, with one extra rule:

1. Use inverse operations to isolate x (same as equations).
2. If you multiply or divide by a POSITIVE number, the sign stays the same.
3. If you multiply or divide by a NEGATIVE number, FLIP the sign!
4. Express the solution as a range (e.g., x > 3) or on a number line.

blocks.title: 4. Worked Example: Solve -2x + 4 > 10
blocks.content:
**Step 1:** Subtract 4 from both sides: -2x > 6.
**Step 2:** Divide both sides by -2. Since we're dividing by a NEGATIVE, FLIP the sign!
**Step 3:** x < -3.

**Final Answer: x < -3.** (All numbers less than -3 satisfy this inequality.)

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: The absolute number one mistake: forgetting to FLIP the inequality sign when dividing by a negative! If -2x > 6, dividing by -2 gives x < -3, NOT x > -3. This single rule is responsible for more lost marks than any other concept in inequalities. Write 'FLIP!' in big letters next to any step where you divide by a negative number.
